title: If the Neural Tube Does Not Close

scenes.visual: Title: If the Neural Tube Does Not Close. Show a schematic closed tube beside one open at the head and one open at the lower end.

scenes.tts: If the neural tube does not close, part of the brain or spinal cord stays open. Failure at the head end causes anencephaly. At the lower end, it causes open spina bifida. These defects can be fatal or cause weakness or paralysis. Closure happens by the end of about the fourth week after fertilization, often before a woman knows she is pregnant. Folic acid taken before conception lowers the risk of many of these defects.

scenes.visual: Lead with a schematic head-to-tail map of failed closure: label anencephaly at the head and open spina bifida at the lower end. Connect the stakes to exposed brain tissue and an open spinal lesion without graphic imagery. Show closure by about the fourth week after fertilization and a folic-acid prevention marker before conception. Do not imply complete protection.

scenes.tts: The brain and spinal cord begin as the neural plate, a flat sheet on the embryo’s back. It narrows and lengthens. It creases at hinge points, and its edges rise as neural folds. The folds meet and fuse. The tube separates from the skin, which seals over it.

scenes.visual: Animate the normal sequence in a schematic trunk cross-section, with a top-view inset for narrowing and lengthening: neural plate, hinge formation, raised folds, fusion, then separation beneath sealed skin.

scenes.tts: In anencephaly, exposed brain tissue degenerates. Affected babies are stillborn or die soon after birth. In one form of open spina bifida, the cord lies in the lesion. Weakness or paralysis and loss of bladder and bowel control are common.

scenes.visual: Return to the head-versus-lower-end map. For anencephaly, show schematic loss of exposed brain tissue. For open spina bifida, show the cord in the open lesion, labelled myelomeningocele, with the narrated consequences. Do not depict spina bifida occulta as an open tube.

scenes.tts: Randomized trials tested prevention. In women with a previous affected pregnancy, folic acid started before conception cut recurrence by about seventy two percent. A Hungarian trial found no affected pregnancies with a multivitamin containing folic acid, against six in the comparison group. That supports prevention of a first occurrence. But that trial alone could not credit folic acid by itself.

scenes.visual: Show separate trial panels. Recurrence panel: women with a previous affected pregnancy; folic acid before conception; about 72% relative reduction in recurrence. First-occurrence panel: Hungarian multivitamin containing folic acid, no affected pregnancies, versus six with trace elements. Label the multivitamin attribution limit. Avoid presenting 72% as a first-occurrence result or an absolute reduction.

scenes.tts: Now consider one route to closure failure. Convergent extension narrows the plate as cells push between side neighbors. Planar cell polarity gives them a shared direction. If the plate stays too wide, the folds cannot meet.

scenes.visual: Introduce this as one closure mechanism, after prevention. In top view, cells intercalate so a broad plate becomes narrow and long; indicate shared planar polarity with directional marks. Compare folds meeting across a narrow plate with folds stopping short across a wide plate. Use no invented cell counts.

scenes.tts: In frog embryos, researchers disrupted Dishevelled signaling at the plate’s midline. The plate stayed wide. The folds still rose and moved inward, but the tube stayed open.

scenes.visual: Label the animal model as frog. Mark the midline intervention, show failed narrowing followed by raised folds that cannot meet. Do not add injection quantities or experimental instructions.

scenes.tts: Disrupting the sides instead left closure intact. Under those conditions, the signal was needed at the midline, where narrowing sets the distance. In the loop-tail mouse, the midline failed to extend before folding, and closure never started.

scenes.visual: Show the frog lateral-targeting comparison: narrowing and closure remain intact. Place it beside the midline result. Then show separate loop-tail mouse evidence: failed midline extension before neurulation and failure to initiate closure. Keep the species labels visible.

scenes.tts: There are other routes. Diabetes before pregnancy and valproic acid in early pregnancy raise the risk of spina bifida. Most mothers of affected babies are not folate deficient by ordinary tests. How folate prevents defects is not settled. Its benefit is clear: lower risk, with some defects still occurring.

scenes.visual: Close with multiple contributing routes: maternal diabetes before pregnancy, valproic acid in early pregnancy, and the already illustrated polarity mechanism. State that ordinary measured folate deficiency does not explain all affected pregnancies. End on folic acid lowering risk, with incomplete protection and an unresolved mechanism. Do not imply a universal single cause or advise medication changes.
Closing card: Early closure. Serious defects when it fails. Folic acid before conception lowers risk. Retain the closing pause.
